SPRINT 66 (V0.29.20) -- US-498 (S5 closeout/shutdown splash) DONE, 4/7.
THE HEADLINE LESSON: REVERSING AN ANIMATION IS TWO REVERSALS, AND SHIPPING ONE OF THEM IS A BLACK SCREEN. The kit flipped `animation-direction: reverse` on every class with a comment saying 'the keyframes are symmetric enough that reverse just works'. Direction was the easy half; the running ORDER also has to reverse. The boot timeline ENDS with a fadeout DELAYED 6s, and `animation-fill-mode: both` holds the reversed animation's FIRST RELEVANT keyframe through that delay -- which for direction:reverse is `to`, i.e. opacity 0. So the fill-mode that exists to prevent a flash of unstyled content pinned the mark invisible for 6 seconds of a 7-SECOND GRACE WINDOW (pi.powerWatch.smoothingSec): black for essentially the whole shutdown. Fix = reversed delay is T - (bootDelay + bootDuration), T = 6.5s; derived from splash.svg, no invented numbers, and the test RE-DERIVES them so re-timing the boot re-aims the closeout.
NOTE THE SHAPE OF THE BUG, because it will recur: three individually-correct declarations (a delay, a fill-mode, a direction) interacting. Every part had a passing test. Every surrounding component worked -- sequencer emitted, emitter wrote, .path watched the right file, server served the right page with the token, JS revealed the stage on time. The surface it revealed was black. When a UI 'does nothing' and all the parts test green, stop testing parts and start SAMPLING THE OUTPUT ON A CLOCK.
SO THAT IS WHAT THE TEST DOES: tests/ui/test_shutdown_splash_render.py resolves the shipped CSS (cascade + !important, comma-list shorthands, fill-mode/direction/delay) and samples the mark's opacity every 250ms across the real grace window read from config. RED naming every blank instant t=[1.0..6.0]. One assertion I wrote OVER-CLAIMED -- 'brightness never rises' failed on the DESIGNED throb, whose recovery genuinely raises brightness -- and I corrected the test to the honest envelope claim (max->low endpoints, second half never brighter than the first) rather than keeping a green-looking lie. Fidelity limit is stated in the file: easings treated as linear, so endpoints and the SIGN of a change are exact, mid-segment values are not; every assertion is zero-vs-nonzero or an endpoint.
A KEEP-LIST IS A COST, NOT A SAFETY NET -- the deploy half, and it generalises. US-495 keep-listed the closeout surface as 'the kit's install.sh owns those'. But a keep-listed asset is never installed, never pruned and never byte-verified; its only refresh path was the A-9 kiosk step, which is ALLOWED TO WARN AND SKIP (install.sh aborts if it cannot detect session type or chromium). So the stale hole US-495 closed for boot was still open for shutdown -- where it only shows itself DURING a shutdown, nobody watching, no re-run. Moved the whole surface into the manifest (both installers copy identical bytes from the same synced kit, so ownership costs nothing and buys the verify). Keep-list is now version.txt alone, which earns it: the deploy GENERATES it, so the manifest cannot name it. Ask of any keep-list entry: who verifies this, and are they allowed to skip?
WIRING PINS, green on arrival and labelled as such (contract pins, not a TDD claim): tests/pi/splash/test_shutdown_splash_wiring.py drives a REAL sequencer grace into a real states dir, serves the REAL kit over the REAL states_http, and fetches the page at the URL extracted FROM THE SHIPPED UNIT FILE -- nothing asserted against a literal a rename would leave behind on both sides. US-494's lesson one story later.
TD-069 FILED, READ IT BEFORE THE ON-PI CHECK: nothing ever REMOVES shutdown-state. /run is tmpfs, so a CANCELLED grace (the common case -- that is what smoothing is for) leaves phase:cancelled on disk for the rest of the uptime and PathExists has no false->true transition left: the SECOND grace of a boot gets NO closeout splash. I also SUSPECT but did NOT confirm a systemd re-trigger loop on the cancel path -- stated as unverified, not asserted. Root: the file has a write lifecycle and no clear lifecycle. Fix is producer-side (the power path that bricked the Pi once, I-038) -> Atlas decision, not a drive-by edit in a render story.
BL-026 FILED: US-478 + US-497 are DOUBLE-gated and I refused them rather than fake progress. (1) hardware -- no 0x69 on the bus (AI-005, CIO); (2) and the one that matters more, the states/imu SHAPE is still gated on Atlas Q-A (derived-field contract) + Q-B (higher-rate transport). Building a heading/grade/tilt-comp bridge to an unconfirmed contract with no hardware = inventing the numeric contract then testing against my own invention. US-499 (S6) is unblocked and is the highest-value story left: S1/S2/S3/S5 have EVERY ONE of them ended with an owed on-Pi render check, which is exactly the gap S6 closes.

--- PRIOR (US-496, S3 Pi-local cards live + honest-gray) ---

THE HEADLINE LESSON: A HIDE IS NOT A FREE STYLING CHANGE -- IT CHANGES THE GEOMETRY. AC-3 asks for one card to be hidden rather than grayed; because #track is a flex row of full-width cards and US-495's [hidden] guard genuinely removes the element, a hidden card takes NO SLOT. So translateX, the page dots, the swipe, and the "where do I land if the card I am on vanishes" recovery all had to start counting VISIBLE cards (new pure visualPosition / nextVisibleIndex / nearestVisibleIndex; goTo() now refuses a hidden target; a hidden card owns no dot, because a dot navigating nowhere is the same dead affordance as the card behind it). If you gate another card that math is already there -- but the FEEL of it is an on-Pi check, not a unit test.
AND THE FRAGILITY THAT CAME WITH IT: the whole gate rests on `hidden` removing the card from flow, which only works because US-495's guard wins on IMPORTANCE. Adding `!important` to .card or .dot's `display` would tie importance, hand the win to the later same-specificity selector, and silently restore a gated card to the track -- the US-495 defect again, from a one-word edit. There is now a test forbidding it. NOTE for US-499/S6: the US-495 guard test only enumerates elements the MARKUP ships `hidden`; the page dots are JS-CREATED, so the real cascade over them is still unexercised. That, plus the visible-index geometry, is the highest-value thing S6 can render for real.
GRAY vs HIDDEN IS A REAL DISTINCTION, worth carrying: gray says "this instrument is BROKEN"; hidden says "it does not APPLY right now". On a bench with no car, a grayed fuel-trim card is a false fault report. Hence the gate demands an EXPLICIT source.obd.available === true -- deliberately STRICTER than sourceUnavailable(), whose absent-source-block-means-available default is right for "should I gray this tile?" and WRONG for "should I reveal a vehicle card?". THIS SPRINT HAS NOW FOUND THE SAME UNDERLYING BUG THREE STORIES RUNNING (US-492 guard-down banner, US-494 OBD_STARTING, US-496 here): a reading NOT TAKEN rendered as a confident state. Treat `X or <plausible-default>` and any absent-means-fine default as a code smell on sight, and ask whether the consumer needs "gray it" or "reveal it" semantics -- they need OPPOSITE defaults.
JUDGEMENT CALL, PM/ATLAS PLEASE CONFIRM: AC-3 names a "Live Engine Data card" that does not exist yet (Atlas: Slice 2), so I built the MECHANISM and applied it to LTFT rather than DELETING that card. Atlas's design says "remove from carousel now"; the story's conditionalOutcome says "leave it out of the always-present set ... do not fake it". Gating satisfies both readings, keeps code Slice 2 may revive, and exercises the seam Live Engine Data will inherit. Bench observable is identical to the AC (no vehicle card).
LIGHT CARD (it did not exist -- this was the real build). A pure consumer of the SAME states/light file that drives the auto-dim, so I made the tick resolve ONE clock for both the card's freshness verdict and the applied brightness -- otherwise card and screen could disagree by a poll interval about whether the feed is stale. Also DEDUPED the fetch (the tick already fetched `light` for brightness; a naive card would poll the same file twice per tick at 4 Hz). TWO tiles, and THE OMISSION IS THE DESIGN: AMBIENT (reading + read age) and CONDITION (DARK/DIM/DAYLIGHT). I did NOT add the screen-brightness percent, though it was the obvious third tile -- a live STOP holds the surface at FULL regardless of lux (US-484-b ch.4), so a lux-derived percent would contradict the actual screen exactly when it matters most. CONDITION resolves against the SAME injected luxMin/luxFull: a NAME for existing grounded thresholds, never a third set of numbers (proven with a config override, so the values are read, not baked in). The three gray REASONS are distinct on purpose -- "no reading ever arrived" vs "readings stopped arriving" vs "undated" are different faults and the operator needs to know which. No config change needed: pi.sensors.light.enabled was already true (V0.29.15).
DTC NO-DATA was NARROWER than it looks: empty-available ALREADY rendered a calm gray "No stored codes", and the phantom red was S2's CSS bug. The only real gap was an ABSENT state rendering the bare word "unavailable" -> added noDataView(name) for the two cards whose SILENCE is dangerous to misread (dtc: "no data -- codes not read", never an all-clear; light: "no data -- light feed absent", not "dark"). Deliberately NOT applied to the other three (scope fence). Kept alertsCardView(null) === null -- tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py:1017 pins it, and the SHELL is the right single place to decide absence for every card.
GREEN (synchronous, in-loop): 282 passed -- tests/ui 233 (33 new) + test_dashboard_kit 49; ruff clean on both touched Python files; carousel.js parses under node (every probe-driven test requires the module). Bumped test_dashboard_kit's card-slot count 4 -> 5. NO Python SOURCE changed, so tests/pi cannot have regressed.
